headings.title: Supervision of correctional centers and parole
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Department of Corrections to supervise and manage all state correctional centers and probation and parole services.

headings.title: Divisions and board composing department
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the composition of the department consisting of the parole board and four specialized operational divisions.

headings.title: Subdivision of divisions into sections
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department director to subdivide each division into sections, bureaus, or offices necessary to carry out statutory duties.

headings.title: Women offender program and director duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to operate a women offender program supervised by a director of women's programs providing gender-responsive and trauma-informed supervision and services.

headings.title: Advisory committee on women offender programs
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an advisory committee under the director of women's programs, including the directors of the office on women's health and mental health (or designee) and four appointees, to address women's criminal justice needs.

entries.reviewSummary: Department of Corrections administrative structure, operational divisions, women offender program, and advisory committee.

headings.title: Community behavioral health program establishment
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish a comprehensive community behavioral health program for supervised individuals with serious behavioral health conditions.

headings.title: Interagency collaboration on eligibility and oversight
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC in collaboration with DMH to establish referral, evaluation, eligibility, discharge, and multidisciplinary oversight, auditing, and reporting processes.

headings.title: Mental health provider contracts and reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Requires DMH in collaboration with DOC to contract with, pay, and monitor behavioral health providers accepting all eligible referrals on a per-month, per-referral pay-for-performance model and billing third parties.

entries.reviewSummary: Community behavioral health program for supervised individuals with serious behavioral health conditions, interagency oversight, and Mental Health provider contracts.

headings.title: Prison impact statements required with fiscal notes
headings.reviewNote: Requires a prison impact statement to accompany the fiscal note of any legislation affecting the number of persons supervised by DOC or any department program or service.

headings.title: Preparation, timing, and required contents of statements
headings.reviewNote: Directs DOC, in consultation with legislative research oversight, to furnish prison impact statements before committee hearings and perfection, projecting populations, ten-year fiscal impact, cost factors, and methodologies.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory prison impact statements accompanying fiscal notes for legislation affecting department populations, programs, or services.

headings.title: Supervision of department and appointment of director
headings.reviewNote: Vests general supervision, management, and control of DOC in the director of corrections, appointed by the governor with the advice and consent of the senate.

headings.title: Qualifications, oath, bond, and primary responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Sets character, correctional management experience, U.S. citizenship (Missouri residency not required at appointment), oath, surety bond, full-time duty, public safety primary duty, and rehabilitative secondary duty.

headings.title: Employee duties, work supervision, and uniform policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to establish employee duties, supervise work assignments, implement uniform policies for offenders and staff, and permits requiring employee conduct reports.

headings.title: Control and jurisdiction over committed persons
headings.reviewNote: Grants the director control and jurisdiction over all persons legally sentenced, assigned, and committed to the custody and supervision of the department.

headings.title: Control over department property and correctional centers
headings.reviewNote: Grants the director control and jurisdiction over all department real estate, buildings, equipment, correctional centers, and products, except where reserved to others by law.

headings.title: Rules, regulations, orders, and findings
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to make and enforce rules, regulations, orders, and findings deemed necessary for managing correctional centers and persons under department control.

headings.title: Segregation of male and female offenders and classification
headings.reviewNote: Requires establishing and maintaining correctional centers and units, as provided by appropriations, to segregate male and female offenders and classify offenders by security, supervision, and program needs.

headings.title: Annual budget preparation and submission
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to prepare and submit an annual budget detailing all funds necessary for department and divisional operations.

headings.title: Written administrative report and improvement advice
headings.reviewNote: Requires a written administrative report to the governor and general assembly (which may include plans and financial summaries) and requires advising the governor and joint committee on corrections on improvements.

headings.title: Development of long-range operational plan
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to initiate and oversee long-range comprehensive planning for all departmental correctional programs.

entries.reviewSummary: Appointment, qualifications, oath, bond, administrative duties, institutional control, budgeting, and reporting of the department director.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority under administrative procedures act
headings.reviewNote: Grants the department rulemaking authority to adopt and amend regulations pursuant to chapter 536 and section 536.024.

headings.title: Department internal management policies and inspection
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to adopt internal management policies and operating regulations exempt from Missouri Register and CSR publication but available for public inspection and review.

headings.title: Division internal management policies and regulations
headings.reviewNote: Requires department divisions to jointly or separately adopt internal management regulations, policies, and procedures consistent with department policies without chapter 536 publication.

headings.title: Correctional center orders and operational rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs chief administrative officers of correctional centers to establish local operating orders and unit rules consistent with department policy.

entries.reviewSummary: Department rulemaking authority under chapter 536 and internal operational management regulations for correctional centers.

headings.title: Arrangements for receipt of federal funds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to enter into arrangements with the federal government to receive and disburse federal funds subject to appropriations and requires submitting required plans and reports.

headings.title: Director approval of federal assistance applications
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to approve advisable federal assistance applications administered through the department after consultation with the appropriate division director.

headings.title: Receipt and disbursement of appropriated funds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to receive and disburse other public and appropriated funds directed by the general assembly.

entries.reviewSummary: Department authority to apply for, receive, and disburse federal and legislative funds for correctional purposes.

headings.title: Volunteer recruitment and citizen involvement programs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department and its divisions to recruit, train, and accept citizen volunteers to supplement correctional programs.

headings.title: Compliance with department volunteer policy regulations
headings.reviewNote: Requires all citizen volunteers to comply with applicable department and division policy regulations during service.

headings.title: Division management and written volunteer rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires divisions using volunteers to provide supervisory staff, develop written guidelines, and recognize exceptional volunteer service.

headings.title: Volunteer status as unpaid state employees
headings.reviewNote: Accords volunteers the legal status of unpaid state employees protected by workers compensation and the legal expense fund.

headings.title: Expense reimbursement and state vehicle usage
headings.reviewNote: Permits reimbursing transportation and necessary expenses for volunteers on special assignment from regular appropriations and permits state vehicle use under staff rules.

headings.title: Termination of volunteer service and review right
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to terminate any volunteer, who shall receive a written statement of reasons and, upon request, a review of the termination.

entries.reviewSummary: Correctional volunteer programs, division management duties, unpaid employee protections, travel reimbursement, and volunteer termination review.

headings.title: Offender records as public records and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Designates all department offender records as public records under chapter 610 except personal medical history, records closed by federal or state law, and internal security administrative reports.

headings.title: Discretionary inspection of reports by offender
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court of jurisdiction or the department at their discretion to allow an offender to inspect department reports when in the offender's best interest or welfare.

headings.title: Automated records access for agencies and research
headings.reviewNote: Permits automating department records and making them available to treatment agencies, law enforcement agencies, or qualified researchers under written confidentiality agreements.

headings.title: Employee access limits and confidentiality rules
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits department employee access to closed material unless necessary for duties and directs the department by rule to determine authorized access and confidentiality procedures.

headings.title: Commercial or political use of names prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person or entity from knowingly soliciting, disclosing, receiving, publishing, or using any name or list of names for commercial or political purposes in violation of this section.

headings.title: Provider duty to furnish offender medical records
headings.reviewNote: Requires health care providers and hospitals that cared for incarcerated offenders to provide copies of medical records upon demand from the health care administrator, with reasonable copy compensation and confidentiality immunity.

headings.title: Admissibility of certified copies of records
headings.reviewNote: Makes properly certified copies of department records admissible as evidence in all courts and administrative tribunals when designated public under chapter 610 or declared admissible by the court or tribunal.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Makes any person found guilty of violating any provision of this section guilty of a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Public-record status of offender records with closed-record exceptions, discretionary inspection, automated sharing, medical record copies, certified evidence, and misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Use of correctional buildings for compatible activities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes granting the use of correctional center buildings and grounds to governmental, private, or nonprofit entities for compatible activities.

headings.title: Lease of buildings through commissioner of administration
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department director to notify the commissioner of administration, who may lease such buildings or grounds pursuant to public bid to governmental, private, or nonprofit entities.

headings.title: Charges for utilities and furnished services
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to charge lessees at a minimum for the costs of utilities and services furnished to the leased facility.

headings.title: Lease terms, renewal options, and state indemnification
headings.reviewNote: Restricts lease terms to one year or less with renewal options, requiring compatible maintenance and state liability protections.

headings.title: Execution of lease agreements on behalf of state
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director of the department of corrections to execute leases on behalf of the state.

entries.reviewSummary: Leasing of correctional facility buildings and grounds for compatible public or nonprofit uses and lease terms.

headings.title: Workers compensation coverage for department personnel
headings.reviewNote: Extends the provisions of chapter 287 governing workers compensation to all department personnel, with the state acting as self-insurer.

headings.title: Tort liability disclaimer and legal obligations
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that extending workers compensation coverage does not create general tort liability against the department or state.

entries.reviewSummary: Workers compensation coverage for all department employees and limitation of state tort liability.

headings.title: Financial interest in department vendors prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits department employees from knowingly holding financial or business interests in vendors providing goods or services to the department.

headings.title: Financial business with offenders or families prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits department employees from knowingly having financial business with any offender committed to or supervised by the department or with the offender's family members.

headings.title: Conversion of department property prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Except as provided by section 217.135, prohibits department employees from taking, removing, using, converting, or selling department property, provisions, natural resources, goods, or articles of value.

headings.title: Dismissal and disciplinary grounds for violations
headings.reviewNote: Designates violations of employee business and property restrictions as grounds for dismissal or appropriate administrative discipline.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibitions on employee business connections, transactions with offenders, conversion of property, and disciplinary sanctions.

headings.title: Receiving unauthorized gifts from offenders prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Designates the unauthorized receipt of gifts, money, or services from offenders or their families by employees as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Bribery for procuring pardon or parole prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Designates receiving anything of value for procuring or assisting to procure a pardon or parole as a class B felony offense.

headings.title: Duty of employees to report bribery violations
headings.reviewNote: Requires department employees aware of any violation of this section to report it to the director, with failure to report being grounds for dismissal or other appropriate disciplinary action.

headings.title: Director investigation and referral to prosecutor
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to investigate suspected bribery offenses and report findings and witnesses to the appropriate prosecuting attorney.

entries.reviewSummary: Criminal penalties for bribery, unauthorized receipt of gifts from offenders, mandatory reporting, and prosecutor referrals.

headings.title: Pilot treatment program for child sex offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to design and implement a pilot community corrections treatment program patterned after Oregon's Restitution, Treatment and Training program for child sex offenders, with costs paid by court-referred participants.

headings.title: Implementation deadline and annual effectiveness report
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to implement the pilot program by January 1, 1992, and report annually on its effectiveness to the governor, house speaker, and senate president pro tem.

entries.reviewSummary: Pilot community corrections treatment program for sexual offenders of children patterned after Oregon's program, offender-paid costs, and annual reporting.

headings.title: Electrified security fence systems at correctional centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to install high voltage electrified security fence systems at all existing and proposed maximum security centers and permits discretionary installation at medium security centers.

headings.title: Safety precautions for community and personnel
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to take all reasonable and necessary precautions consistent with industry standards to protect the safety of the local community and department personnel.

entries.reviewSummary: Installation of high voltage electrified security fence systems at maximum and medium security correctional centers and safety precautions.

headings.title: Sentencing and corrections oversight commission established
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the sentencing and corrections oversight commission and designates its legislative, judicial, and corrections membership.

headings.title: Staggered four-year terms for appointed members
headings.reviewNote: Provides for staggered four-year terms for appointed members of the commission and filling of vacancies for unexpired terms.

headings.title: Bylaws, meeting schedules, and co-chair duties
headings.reviewNote: Establishes duties of legislative co-chairs for convening meetings at least twice annually and adopting administrative bylaws.

headings.title: Commission duties and recidivism reduction evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to monitor earned compliance credits, reinvest cost savings, and examine crime victim restitution collections.

headings.title: Department and court data collection requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, board, and office of state courts administrator (source footnote notes word 'court' appears in original rolls) to collect and report requested data timely.

headings.title: Annual report to legislative and judicial leaders
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual reports beginning December 31, 2013, to legislative, judicial, and executive leaders on statutory effects, and permits recommendations on reinvesting savings and policy changes.

headings.title: Department administrative support for commission
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Department of Corrections to provide necessary administrative and clerical support to the oversight commission.

headings.title: Expense reimbursement without member compensation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that members serve without compensation but receive reimbursement for actual and necessary travel expenses.

headings.title: Automatic expiration on August 28, 2018
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the section automatically expires on August 28, 2018 (source note records 'Expires 8-28-18').

entries.reviewSummary: Creation, membership, duties, annual reporting, and August 28, 2018 expiration of the sentencing and corrections oversight commission.

headings.title: Definitions of extraordinary circumstances and postpartum
headings.reviewNote: Defines extraordinary circumstance, labor, postpartum, and restraints for the custody and transport of pregnant offenders.

headings.title: Prohibition on restraints for pregnant offenders
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits correctional centers from using restraints on a third-trimester pregnant offender during transport, medical appointments, labor, delivery, or 48 hours postdelivery unless a corrections officer determines extraordinary circumstances exist.

headings.title: Documentation requirements when restraints are necessary
headings.reviewNote: Requires written documentation within forty-eight hours justifying extraordinary circumstances when restraints are used, retained for ten years.

headings.title: Least restrictive restraints and mechanical restraint bans
headings.reviewNote: Requires any authorized restraints to be the least restrictive and most reasonable available, bans leg, ankle, waist, or mechanical restraints, and requires front-placed wrist restraints if used.

headings.title: Removal of restraints upon medical provider request
headings.reviewNote: Mandates immediate removal of all restraints upon request by a treating doctor, nurse, or health care professional.

headings.title: Vehicle seatbelt requirement for pregnant offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires pregnant offenders to be transported in vehicles equipped with seatbelts.

headings.title: Biannual review of restraint documentation reports
headings.reviewNote: Directs biannual review of all restraint incident reports by the oversight commission and women's advisory committee.

headings.title: Employee training and notice to female offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires each facility's chief administrative officer to provide employee training (which may be online) on this section and section 217.147, inform female offenders orally and in writing upon admission, include policies in handbooks, and post notices.

headings.title: Applicability limited to department of corrections
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the provisions of this section apply only to the department of corrections.

entries.reviewSummary: Limitations on physical restraints for pregnant third-trimester and 48-hour postpartum offenders, documentation, medical overrides, biannual reviews, training, notice, and DOC-only scope.

headings.title: Division director appointing authority under chapter 36
headings.reviewNote: Requires any division director, subject to the department director's supervision, to exercise chapter 36 appointing authority powers and duties to employ division personnel.

headings.title: Qualifications and citizenship of division director
headings.reviewNote: Requires a division director to have recognized character, integrity, and appropriate education, training, and experience, and to be a U.S. citizen (Missouri citizenship not required at appointment).

headings.title: Full-time employment and outside compensation ban
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division director to be a full-time employee of the division holding no other regular, compensated position while serving.

entries.reviewSummary: Division director appointing authority under chapter 36, character and citizenship qualifications, and full-time employment requirement.

headings.title: Establishment and operation of inmate canteens
headings.reviewNote: Permits the chief administrative officer of any correctional center operated by the division, with department director approval, to establish and operate an offender canteen or commissary.

headings.title: Inmate canteen fund creation and allowable expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Inmate Canteen Fund in the state treasury, pays acquisition and operating costs from it, dedicates proceeds and interest solely to recreational, religious, educational, or reentry services, and exempts balances from biennial reversion under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Operation of correctional center inmate canteens and dedication of canteen fund proceeds for offender welfare.

headings.title: Regulation of offender personal property by policy
headings.reviewNote: Directs that the allowable amount and volume of personal property possessed by offenders in correctional centers be established by policy.

headings.title: Impoundment and disposal of unauthorized property
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the impoundment and disposal of unauthorized personal property found in an offender's possession pursuant to policy directives.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulation of personal property possession in correctional centers and impoundment of unauthorized items.

headings.title: Definitions of appropriate quantity and hygiene products
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'appropriate quantity' (daily amount satisfying individual need for intended purpose) and 'feminine hygiene products' (tampons and sanitary napkins).

headings.title: Provision of feminine hygiene products at no cost
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to ensure an appropriate quantity of feminine hygiene products conforming to applicable industry standards is available at no cost to confined female offenders.

headings.title: Legislative appropriations to support product distribution
headings.reviewNote: Permits the general assembly to appropriate funds to assist the director in satisfying the section's requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Requirements for providing feminine hygiene products at no cost to female offenders confined in correctional centers.

headings.title: Determination of maximum correctional center capacity
headings.reviewNote: Directs that the maximum inmate capacity of each correctional center shall be determined by the director of the department.

headings.title: Emergency assignment of offenders beyond capacity
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits assigning offenders to a correctional center at maximum capacity except upon a formal declaration of emergency by the director.

entries.reviewSummary: Determination of maximum correctional center capacity and emergency offender assignment authority.

headings.title: Custody of federal prisoners in state centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department director, when practicable, to receive criminals convicted of federal law violations and sentenced by U.S. courts, and permits retaining custody until discharged by due process.

headings.title: Federal government liability for prisoner support expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires the United States government to pay the expenses of offender support and execution of federal sentences in state centers.

headings.title: Prosecution of federal prisoners for escape
headings.reviewNote: Subjects federal prisoners who escape or attempt to escape from a state correctional center to prosecution as if committed under state authority.

headings.title: Liability of correctional officers for prisoner neglect
headings.reviewNote: Holds correctional facility chief administrative officers liable for neglect of duty regarding federal prisoners under state penalty laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Admittance and housing of federal prisoners in state correctional centers, federal expense obligations, and escape liabilities.

headings.title: Designation of clothing for confined offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires the chief administrative officer of each correctional center, with division director approval, to designate offender clothing by rule and regulation.

headings.title: Nutritious food diet and deprivation penalty ban
headings.reviewNote: Requires providing all confined offenders with a sufficient quantity of wholesome food and strictly prohibits using food deprivation as punishment.

headings.title: Monitoring and reporting on food, clothing, and health
headings.reviewNote: Requires the chief administrative officer to keep advised on the quantity and quality of food and clothing and on offender health, condition, and safekeeping, and to report findings to the director.

entries.reviewSummary: Designation of offender clothing, requirement for wholesome food without food deprivation as discipline, and chief administrative officer monitoring and reporting.

headings.title: System of compensation for offender work and education
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to adopt regulations establishing an offender compensation system for institutional labor and educational progress.

headings.title: Preparation of graduated wage schedules for offenders
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to prepare graduated wage schedules for payment of compensation to offenders.

headings.title: Standard eight-hour work day for offender labor
headings.reviewNote: Establishes eight hours of work per day as the standard day of labor for offenders, absent emergencies or official authorization.

headings.title: Deductions from offender compensation for victim restitution
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to pay into the crime victims' compensation fund from an offender's compensation or account any amount owed to the fund that the offender failed to pay before entering a correctional center.

headings.title: Deductions for willful destruction of state property
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes deducting sums from offender earnings to pay restitution for willful or malicious damage to state property.

headings.title: Approval requirement for paid work and confiscation
headings.reviewNote: Restricts compensation solely to approved work assignments and authorizes confiscation of unauthorized earnings for the crime victims fund.

entries.reviewSummary: System of offender labor compensation, graduated wage schedules, standard hours, and authorized deductions for restitution.

headings.title: Monthly crediting of offender earnings
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to credit earnings from labor or educational participation to offender accounts at least monthly.

headings.title: Expenditure of earnings for approved necessities
headings.reviewNote: Permits offenders to use credited earnings to purchase approved personal necessities not furnished by the division.

headings.title: Use of earnings for dependent family support
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes chief administrative officers upon offender consent to disburse compensation for the support of family dependents.

headings.title: Prohibition on fund transfers between offenders
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits offenders from transferring funds from their accounts to any other offenders.

headings.title: Minimum savings account balances for work release
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to establish a schedule of minimum balances for each offender savings account established through a work release program or halfway house operation.

headings.title: Offset of offender accounts for state indebtedness
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to reduce offender account balances to satisfy indebtedness owed to the state.

entries.reviewSummary: Offender earnings administration, authorized expenditures for necessities and family support, transfer bans, and state debt offsets.

headings.title: Sanctions for frivolous lawsuits and false testimony
headings.reviewNote: Mandates adding sixty days to initial parole eligibility or deducting up to fifty percent of account balances for frivolous lawsuits or false testimony.

headings.title: Disciplinary conduct violation rules for litigation abuse
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to promulgate rules making litigation abuse and false filings conduct violations subject to discipline.

headings.title: Maximum term of imprisonment unaffected by sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that court-ordered maximum terms of imprisonment cannot be extended by administrative litigation sanctions.

headings.title: Minimum ten-dollar balance retained in account
headings.reviewNote: Protects a minimum account balance of ten dollars from deduction for litigation abuse sanctions, allowing future compensation deductions.

entries.reviewSummary: Sanctions against offenders filing frivolous lawsuits or false testimony, account deductions, parole delays, and minimum balance protections.

headings.title: Visitor permission and regulation in correctional centers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits entry into correctional centers except by special permission of institutional administrators under departmental regulations.

headings.title: Authorized state officials permitted to visit facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes designated state officials, judges, legislators, and prosecutors to visit correctional centers at any time, and their assistants at any reasonable time when authorized by superiors under department rules.

headings.title: Clergy visitation privileges and religious rites administration
headings.reviewNote: Grants recognized clergy access to visit offenders and administer religious rites subject to facility safety and security rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulation of visitors to correctional centers, authorized visits by state officials, and clergy access rights.

headings.title: Unauthorized delivery of letters and items prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Restricts bringing letters, writings, or articles of value into or out of correctional centers solely to designated personnel.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for unauthorized delivery
headings.reviewNote: Designates unauthorized transmission of letters or articles to or from offenders as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibition against carrying unauthorized letters or articles into or out of correctional centers and misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Carrying of firearms by designated department employees
headings.reviewNote: Permits designated department employees under department rules to carry firearms when necessary for discharging duties in Missouri or any state.

headings.title: Law enforcement arrest powers for escaped offenders
headings.reviewNote: Grants authorized department personnel full law enforcement powers to arrest escaped offenders and apprehend persons aiding escapes.

entries.reviewSummary: Authority of designated department employees to carry firearms and exercise law enforcement arrest powers for escaping offenders.

headings.title: Establishment of reception and diagnostic centers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish reception and diagnostic centers for individuals committed to state correctional custody.

headings.title: Offender commitments delivered to designated centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires all legal commitments to be made to the department, with delivery of offenders to the center designated by the director.

headings.title: Study, evaluation, and classification of committed persons
headings.reviewNote: Charges reception and diagnostic centers with the study, evaluation, and classification of all persons committed to the department.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishment of reception and diagnostic centers for the examination, study, and classification of all committed offenders.

headings.title: Delivery of committed offenders by county sheriffs
headings.reviewNote: Directs county sheriffs or delivering officers to deliver committed offenders to reception centers and receive delivery certificates.

headings.title: Required legal, health, and sentence documentation
headings.reviewNote: Requires written or electronic delivery of standardized sentence copy, prosecutor crime/victim/history information (source footnote notes word 'know' appears in original rolls for 'known'), and sheriff jail health records and jail-time credit certification.

headings.title: Department authority to refuse incomplete deliveries
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the department to refuse acceptance of any offender delivered without complete mandatory legal and health documentation.

entries.reviewSummary: Procedures for sheriff delivery of offenders to reception centers, mandatory sentencing and medical documentation, and refusal rights.

headings.title: Medical examination by licensed physician upon delivery
headings.reviewNote: Requires every newly delivered offender to undergo an examination by a licensed physician upon arrival at a diagnostic center.

headings.title: Recording of physical characteristics and identification data
headings.reviewNote: Mandates accurate recording of the offender's legal name, age, physical dimensions, complexion, and distinct identifying physical marks.

entries.reviewSummary: Initial medical examinations by licensed physicians upon reception and recording of comprehensive physical identification data.

headings.title: Diagnostic testing and correctional center assignment
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to conduct established diagnostic examinations and assign offenders to appropriate correctional centers.

headings.title: Transmission of diagnostic report and recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Requires reception centers to deliver detailed diagnostic findings and treatment recommendations to the receiving facility.

entries.reviewSummary: Diagnostic examinations and testing of new offenders and transmission of classification reports to assigned correctional centers.

headings.title: Establishment and composition of classification teams
headings.reviewNote: Directs the establishment of institutional classification teams composed of the offender and three to five appointed staff members.

headings.title: Duties and recommendations of classification teams
headings.reviewNote: Charges classification teams with reviewing diagnostic reports, recommending custody and work assignments, and monitoring rehabilitation progress.

headings.title: Offender assignment based on department assessment
headings.reviewNote: Requires that institutional assignments be determined according to security and programming needs assessed through department systems.

entries.reviewSummary: Composition and responsibilities of facility classification teams evaluating custody, program assignments, and rehabilitation progress.

headings.title: Mandatory adherence to schedule of prescribed activities
headings.reviewNote: Requires general population offenders to adhere to prescribed schedules of academic education, vocational training, treatment, and work.

headings.title: Exemption from scheduled activities for validated reasons
headings.reviewNote: Permits excusing an offender from assigned activities upon establishing valid cause approved by the facility chief administrative officer.

entries.reviewSummary: Requirements for general population offenders to adhere to assigned work and treatment schedules and procedures for validated exemptions.

headings.title: Treatment programs for first and young offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires establishing specialized correctional treatment programs designed for first offenders and offenders eighteen years of age or younger.

headings.title: Physical separation of offenders under eighteen years
headings.reviewNote: Mandates physical separation of offenders under eighteen years of age from adult offenders and provides educational diploma programs.

headings.title: Rulemaking for separate housing and program space
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rulemaking under section 217.378(2) (source footnote notes section 217.378 was repealed by H.B. 1608, 2013) for under-18 treatment programs, which may include separate housing units or adult-inaccessible space.

headings.title: Contracting authority and acceptance of public funds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes DOC to determine juvenile program participant numbers based on appropriations, permits public or private contracting for under-18 services and facilities, and requires applying for and accepting available public and private funds.

headings.title: Evaluation process for juvenile offender programs
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to develop and maintain an ongoing evaluation process to measure outcomes of juvenile offender programs.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory treatment programs for first offenders and youth under eighteen, physical separation from adult populations, and contracts.

headings.title: Plan of educational instruction for confined offenders
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to develop and implement a comprehensive educational instruction plan for all confined offenders.

headings.title: Curricula, vocational training, and library facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires the educational plan to include grades 1–12 curricula, vocational training courses, and adequate library facilities in each correctional center.

headings.title: Cooperation with state education departments
headings.reviewNote: Requires DESE and the Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development to cooperate by giving advice, counsel, and information so programs meet public and vocational school standards.

headings.title: Mandatory basic education enrollment by 2001
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to require, by January 1, 2001, all general population offenders without a high school education or equivalent to be enrolled in department basic educational programs.

entries.reviewSummary: Offender educational instruction plan, elementary/secondary curricula, vocational courses, facility libraries, education agency cooperation, and mandatory basic education enrollment.

headings.title: Validated risk and need assessment tools
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to adopt streamlined, validated risk and need assessment tools for men and women and review tools and scoring cutoffs every five years for predictive validity across gender and racial groups.

headings.title: Program access, admission criteria, and recidivism tracking
headings.reviewNote: Applies to all DOC-funded programs and requires procedures promoting risk/need prioritization, consistent admission criteria, and recidivism measurement by risk and need level.

headings.title: Evidence-based programs and supervision policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC for supervised offenders to implement evidence-based cognitive-behavioral programs, adopt a behavior response policy for sanctions and incentives, and adopt a risk/need tool readministration policy.

headings.title: Staff training and performance measurement
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC for institutional and community staff to mandate periodic risk/need assessment training, provide client-interaction and case-plan training, and measure staff performance against best practices.

headings.title: Quality assurance protocol for mental health programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to adopt a protocol to collect quality assurance data for community-based mental health treatment programs.

headings.title: Performance metrics for supervision outcomes
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to adopt performance metrics to report on supervision outcomes.

entries.reviewSummary: Department adoption and five-year validation of risk and need assessment tools, program prioritization, supervision policies, staff training, mental health quality data, and outcome metrics.

headings.title: Treatment program for chronic nonviolent substance offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to design and implement an intensive long-term treatment program for chronic nonviolent offenders with serious substance abuse addictions not convicted of a dangerous felony under section 556.061 (version in effect until 1-01-28 per Revisor's note).

headings.title: Pre-sentencing screening, eligibility, and judicial sentencing
headings.reviewNote: Requires pre-sentencing notice and DOC eligibility screening; permits sentencing eligible offenders (except under section 558.019) to 12–24 months institutional treatment with suspended execution of incarceration pending completion.

headings.title: Successful program completion and probationary release review
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division of probation and parole to advise the sentencing court of an offender's probationary release date thirty days prior to release upon successful completion; permits the court to order execution of sentence if probation is not appropriate.

headings.title: Removal for uncooperative participation and sentence execution
headings.reviewNote: Requires removing an offender who has not successfully completed or is not cooperatively participating in the program, advising the court, serving the prescribed sentence, and voiding probation consideration.

headings.title: Prior commitment exclusion for minimum prison term
headings.reviewNote: Excludes initial incarceration in this substance treatment program from being considered a prior prison commitment under section 558.019.

entries.reviewSummary: Chronic nonviolent substance abuse treatment program (in effect until 1-01-28 per Revisor's note), judicial sentencing, probationary release review, removal, and prior commitment exclusion.

headings.title: Treatment program for chronic nonviolent substance offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to design and implement an intensive long-term treatment program for chronic nonviolent offenders with serious substance abuse addictions not convicted of a dangerous felony under section 556.061 (effective 1-01-28, see § 1.901; severability § 1.1005; omits former sub. 5).

headings.title: Pre-sentencing screening, eligibility, and judicial sentencing
headings.reviewNote: Requires pre-sentencing notice and DOC eligibility screening; permits sentencing eligible offenders (except under section 558.019) to 12–24 months institutional treatment with suspended execution of incarceration pending completion.

headings.title: Successful program completion and probationary release review
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division of probation and parole to advise the sentencing court of an offender's probationary release date thirty days prior to release upon successful completion; permits the court to order execution of sentence if probation is not appropriate.

headings.title: Removal for uncooperative participation and sentence execution
headings.reviewNote: Requires removing an offender who has not successfully completed or is not cooperatively participating in the program, advising the court, serving the prescribed sentence, and voiding probation consideration.

entries.reviewSummary: Delayed-effective (1-01-28) version of chronic nonviolent substance abuse treatment program, screening, judicial sentencing, probationary release, and removal (omitting prior commitment exclusion).

headings.title: Offenders under treatment program established by regulation
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish the Offenders Under Treatment Program by regulation as an institutional placement program.

headings.title: Definition of one-hundred-eighty-day treatment program
headings.reviewNote: Defines the program as a 180-day institutional correctional program for monitoring and treating nonviolent substance abuse offenders followed by parole.

headings.title: Eligibility criteria for nonviolent substance offenders
headings.reviewNote: Restricts eligibility to nonviolent first-time offenders convicted of chapter 195 or 579 drug offenses or nonviolent crimes without weapons.

headings.title: Intermediate sanction, parole notification, and release
headings.reviewNote: Designates the program as an intermediate sanction and authorizes the parole board to release successful graduates on parole.

headings.title: Department determination of available institutional space
headings.reviewNote: Provides that institutional bed capacity and program space availability shall be determined by the department of corrections.

headings.title: Removal from program for failure to complete
headings.reviewNote: Requires offenders failing to complete the program to be removed and serve the remainder of their sentences in standard custody.

headings.title: Credit for time served in treatment program
headings.reviewNote: Directs that all time spent in the institutional treatment program shall be credited as time served on the court sentence.

entries.reviewSummary: Intermediate sanction 180-day Offenders Under Treatment Program, eligibility criteria, parole board notifications, and time credit.

headings.title: Grounds for immediate placement and five-day review
headings.reviewNote: Permits immediate placement in complete administrative segregation for immediate security risks, violence, or urgent safety needs, and requires a review hearing within five working days.

headings.title: Periodic review hearings and segregation records
headings.reviewNote: Requires review hearings thirty days after initial confinement and every ninety days thereafter, and directs the chief administrative officer to keep records of names, reasons, duration, and other required information.

headings.title: Access to medical personnel during segregation
headings.reviewNote: Requires that offenders held in administrative segregation have access to medical personnel.

headings.title: Review hearings not contested cases under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Declares that an administrative segregation review hearing under this section is not a contested case under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Grounds for immediate administrative segregation, 5-working-day initial and 30/90-day periodic review hearings, segregation records, medical access, and non-contested case status.

headings.title: Disciplinary violation records entered in central file
headings.reviewNote: Requires detailed recording of institutional rule infractions and disciplinary convictions in the offender file and central department registry.

headings.title: Disciplinary segregation confinement limited to thirty days
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes up to thirty days in disciplinary segregation for rule violations, restricting sentences over ten days to serious conduct infractions.

headings.title: Violation hearings not contested cases and finality
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that disciplinary violation hearings are not contested administrative cases under chapter 536 and orders are unappealable.

entries.reviewSummary: Recording offender conduct violations, limits on disciplinary segregation, and informal unappealable hearing procedures.

headings.title: Violence against employees or other offenders prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits offenders from knowingly committing acts of violence against department employees or other offenders, punishable as a class B felony.

headings.title: Damage to department buildings and property prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits offenders from knowingly damaging buildings or state property owned or operated by the department, punishable as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Class B felony penalties for offender violence against employees or inmates and class D felony penalties for damaging department property.

headings.title: Furnishing unwholesome or unfit food prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of furnishing unfit food to offenders, prohibiting delivering or receiving diseased meat or spoiled provisions.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty for unfit food
headings.reviewNote: Designates the offense of furnishing unfit food to offenders as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Definition of the offense of furnishing or receiving unwholesome or diseased food for offenders and class E felony penalties.

headings.title: Offender abuse by injury or sexual contact
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of offender abuse as knowingly injuring an offender by beating, striking, wounding, or engaging in sexual contact.

headings.title: Class D felony penalty for offender abuse
headings.reviewNote: Designates the crime of offender abuse as a class D felony offense.

headings.title: Use of force by employees strictly limited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits department employees from using physical force on offenders except as necessary for self-defense, suppressing revolts, or maintaining security.

entries.reviewSummary: Definition of offender abuse, class D felony penalty, and strict limitations on employee use of force except for defense and discipline.

headings.title: Duty of employees to report offender abuse
headings.reviewNote: Requires department employees having reasonable cause to believe an offender was abused to report immediately in writing to the director.

headings.title: Mandatory contents of written abuse report
headings.reviewNote: Specifies mandatory contents of abuse reports, including facility details, offender identity, nature of abuse, and complainant information.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for failing to report
headings.reviewNote: Makes any person required by subsection 1 to report who fails to do so within a reasonable time after abuse or neglect guilty of a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Reports by other persons with reasonable cause
headings.reviewNote: Permits any other person with reasonable cause to report suspected offender abuse directly to the director of corrections.

headings.title: Department investigation within twenty-four hours of report
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to initiate an investigation into reported offender abuse within twenty-four hours of receiving the report.

headings.title: Referral of investigative findings to department director
headings.reviewNote: Requires the investigator to refer the complaint and investigative report to the director for appropriate action if the investigation indicates possible abuse.

headings.title: Confidentiality of abuse reports and investigative records
headings.reviewNote: Declares reports made under this section confidential, not public records, and exempt from section 109.180 and chapter 610.

headings.title: Civil and criminal immunity for reporters and witnesses
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil and criminal immunity for making a report or testifying in resulting proceedings, except for perjury liability and unless acting in bad faith or with malicious purpose.

headings.title: Written notice of report receipt and investigation
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying a mandatory reporter in writing within five working days after receipt of the report that it was received and an investigation initiated.

headings.title: Harassment, dismissal, or retaliation prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits anyone directing or exercising authority in a DOC-operated or -funded correctional center from harassing, dismissing, or retaliating against an offender or employee because they or a family member reported a suspected violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory employee reporting of offender abuse, report contents, misdemeanor penalty, permissive public reporting, 24-hour investigation, confidentiality, qualified immunity, receipt notice, and anti-retaliation.

headings.title: Consent or court order for surgery or anesthetic
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits DOC, except in an emergency, from authorizing major surgery or general anesthetic without specific written consent from the offender (or parent/guardian if minor) or an order of the committing or local circuit court.

headings.title: Recommended care and religious beliefs exception
headings.reviewNote: Permits DOC to authorize recommended medical, psychiatric, psychological, surgical, or dental care, but requires specific written consent or court order if contrary to the offender's religious tenets and beliefs.

headings.title: Delegated medical care at non-department facilities
headings.reviewNote: Limits authority of administrators of non-DOC correctional centers to provide medical, psychiatric, psychological, surgical, or dental care to the extent delegated for particular offenders and subject to law.

entries.reviewSummary: Written consent or court order requirements for offender surgery, general anesthetic, and care contrary to religious beliefs, plus delegated medical care at non-department facilities.

headings.title: Prisoner furloughs, permitted purposes, and time limits
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to extend confinement limits for trusted offenders to visit designated in-state places up to thirty days per year for ill relatives, funerals, medical services, job contacts, or rehab, extensible for community release or emergency medical needs.

headings.title: Ten-day advance notice of furlough orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires sending a copy of the director's order to the circuit judge, sheriff, and prosecuting or circuit attorney of the sentencing and visit counties at least ten days in advance, except for funerals or emergency medical furloughs.

entries.reviewSummary: Discretionary prisoner furloughs up to thirty days per year with extension exceptions and ten-day advance notice to local judicial and law enforcement officials.

headings.title: Contracts for residential treatment facilities and sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to contract with public or private entities for residential treatment facilities and community-based sanctions.

headings.title: Contract conditions, inmate fund, and zoning approvals
headings.reviewNote: Establishes mandatory contract standards, facility inspection rules, inmate wage contributions to the Inmate Fund, and municipal zoning approvals.

entries.reviewSummary: Contracts for residential treatment centers and community sanctions, mandatory contract conditions, Inmate Fund, and municipal zoning consent.

headings.title: Work and educational release program establishment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes establishing work and educational release programs for qualifying offenders meeting department standards.

headings.title: Offender wage deductions for maintenance costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires offenders on work release to pay a percentage of their earnings to the Inmate Fund to offset monthly maintenance costs.

headings.title: College educational release expenses paid by offender
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that offenders participating in college educational release programs pay their own educational and school expenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishment of work and educational release programs, offender wage deductions for maintenance, and responsibility for college costs.

headings.title: Offender request for final disposition of detainers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes confined offenders to request final disposition of pending untried indictments, informations, or complaints in Missouri.

headings.title: Lodging of detainers and written notice to offender
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director upon receipt of warrants to lodge detainers and promptly inform offenders in writing of untried charges.

headings.title: Failure of director to notify and speedy trial
headings.reviewNote: Provides that failure of the director to give required notice does not dismiss charges absent violation of constitutional speedy trial rights.

entries.reviewSummary: Right of offenders to request final disposition of untried indictments and detainers, director duties, and speedy trial requirements.

headings.title: House arrest program and eligibility limits
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to establish a house arrest program by rule and permits extending confinement limits for class D or E felony offenders with one year or less before parole, conditional release, or discharge.

headings.title: Continued department custody and rule compliance
headings.reviewNote: Provides that offenders referred to house arrest remain in DOC custody and subject to department rules until released on parole or conditional release by the state parole board.

headings.title: Mandatory work, education, and treatment participation
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOC to mandate participation in work, educational, or vocational programs and other necessary supervision and treatment activities.

headings.title: Restricted absences from residence
headings.reviewNote: Restricts an offender on house arrest to leaving their residence only for the purpose and time necessary to participate in subsection 3 programs and activities.

headings.title: Supervision, electronic surveillance, and arrest warrants
headings.reviewNote: Requires probation and parole supervision (which may use remote electronic surveillance), permits officer arrest warrants and deputizing arresting officers without bail, and permits return to a correctional facility for reclassification.

headings.title: Offender wage payments deposited in inmate fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires house arrest offenders to pay a rule-set percentage of wages up to the program's per capita cost, deposited in the inmate fund to support the house arrest program.

entries.reviewSummary: Department house arrest program for eligible class D or E felony offenders, custody status, required activities, absence limits, probation/parole supervision and arrest warrants, and wage contributions.

headings.title: Failure to return to house arrest offense
headings.reviewNote: Defines the crime of failure to return to house arrest as purposely failing to return to an authorized residence or approved activity.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty for nonreturn
headings.reviewNote: Designates the crime of failure to return to house arrest as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Definition of the crime of failure to return to house arrest and class E felony penalties.

headings.title: House arrest program in St. Louis City
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the jailer of the City of St. Louis to establish a house arrest program for pretrial detainees and sentenced offenders.

headings.title: Jailer rules and extended limits of confinement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the jailer to establish a house arrest program by rule and permits extending confinement limits for pretrial detainees or sentenced persons.

headings.title: Inmate status during city house arrest program
headings.reviewNote: Provides that participants remain in legal inmate status under the custody and rules of the municipal jailer.

headings.title: Mandatory participation in work or education programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating inmates and detainees to participate in work, educational, or treatment programs.

headings.title: Authorized absence restricted to program activities
headings.reviewNote: Restricts authorized absences from residence solely to approved times and activities necessary for program participation.

headings.title: Remote electronic surveillance and revocation authority
headings.reviewNote: Requires jailer supervision and compliance verification (which may use remote electronic surveillance) and permits directing any peace officer to return a participant for violating release conditions.

headings.title: Percentage of inmate wages deducted for costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating inmates to contribute a percentage of their earned wages to pay the costs of house arrest supervision.

headings.title: Escape from custody for failure to return
headings.reviewNote: Designates purposeful failure to return to residence or authorized activity as escape from custody, punishable as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: City of St. Louis jailer house arrest program, remote electronic surveillance, inmate wage contributions, and escape felony penalties.

headings.title: Vocational enterprise program established at correctional centers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to operate a vocational enterprise program including industries, services, training, and agribusinesses at correctional centers.

headings.title: Advisory board approval for establishing new services
headings.reviewNote: Requires prior approval from the advisory board before establishing or renewing vocational services, ensuring benefit to offenders and fair competition.

headings.title: Annual report contents for Missouri vocational enterprises
headings.reviewNote: Specifies mandatory contents for the annual vocational enterprises report, including operations, sales, inmate employment, and financial statements.

entries.reviewSummary: Department vocational enterprise program, industries and agribusinesses, advisory board approval for services, and annual report requirements.

headings.title: Advisory board of vocational enterprises program membership
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Advisory Board of Vocational Enterprises Program, specifies its chair, administrator, labor, manufacturing, criminology, vocational rehabilitation, and ex officio members, and sets staggered four-year terms for public members.

headings.title: Quarterly board meetings called by chairman
headings.reviewNote: Requires the advisory board to meet at least quarterly at the call of the chairman.

headings.title: Advisory duties and director authority over industries
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to advise the director on vocational enterprise planning, services, and manufactured articles, and permits the director to establish or terminate new industries and agribusinesses.

headings.title: Per diem compensation and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Entitles board members, other than the chairman and ex officio members, to $100 per day plus actual and necessary expenses while discharging official duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Advisory Board of Vocational Enterprises Program composition, four-year terms, quarterly meetings, advisory duties, and $100 per diem compensation plus expenses.

headings.title: Procurement of plants, machinery, lands, and buildings
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director under chapters 8 and 34 to provide plants, machinery, equipment, and materials, and permits DOC to lease or purchase lands and buildings for vocational enterprises.

headings.title: Leasing of farm properties and fund deposit
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to lease department-controlled farm properties on fair and reasonable terms, with all proceeds deposited in the working capital revolving fund.

headings.title: Purchase of raw materials and outside help
headings.reviewNote: Permits DOC to purchase raw materials under chapter 34 for industry, service, or agribusiness operations and to employ necessary outside help.

headings.title: Bid waivers for supplies and used equipment purchases
headings.reviewNote: Permits the commissioner of administration to waive competitive bids for open-market enterprise supplies and to purchase used equipment on the open market upon director certification of market value.

headings.title: Distribution of products and enterprise operations
headings.reviewNote: Makes DOC responsible for enterprise goods and services as distributing agent with authority to appoint salespersons, and charges the director with operating facilities and establishing rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Procurement of vocational enterprise plants, machinery, land, and raw materials, farm leasing, open-market bid waivers and used equipment purchases, and product distribution.

headings.title: Contracts with private entities for inmate projects
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to contract with private entities for inmate work or vocational training projects in manufacturing, processing, or service enterprises consistent with rehabilitation.

headings.title: Federal compliance, non-displacement, and board approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires contracts to comply with federal law, be competitively negotiated, not displace civilian workers, and receive approval from the Advisory Board of Vocational Enterprises Program.

headings.title: Leasing correctional building space to private enterprises
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to lease correctional center building space and access real estate to private enterprises, subject to security procedures and all federal and state private business laws.

headings.title: Offender employment and crime victims' fund deductions
headings.reviewNote: Permits lessees, with director approval, to employ and discharge selected offenders subject to department and contractor rules, requiring 5% to 20% of gross wages paid to the crime victims' compensation fund.

headings.title: Wage policies, deduction cap, and FLSA applicability
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to set policies for wages, workers' compensation, and deductions (room/board, taxes, family support) totaling no more than 80% of gross wages, and applies the Fair Labor Standards Act.

entries.reviewSummary: Private entity contracts for inmate work and training projects, correctional facility building leases, offender employment, crime victims' fund wage deductions, and FLSA coverage.

headings.title: Mandatory supply of vocational goods to state
headings.reviewNote: Requires vocational enterprise goods, services, and produce to be furnished upon requisition to the state, public institutions, or private lessors for space leased to state agencies at subsection 4 prices.

headings.title: Nonavailability certificate required for outside purchases
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits state agencies from purchasing covered goods on the open market unless the department certifies nonavailability within ninety days.

headings.title: Interagency cooperation in promoting vocational products
headings.reviewNote: Directs state purchasing and facilities divisions to cooperate in promoting vocational products in state-occupied buildings.

headings.title: Pricing standards not exceeding open market rates
headings.reviewNote: Requires uniform pricing for vocational enterprise products at rates not exceeding fair market prices for like goods.

headings.title: Arbitration of disputes regarding price or quality
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a three-member arbitration process to resolve pricing, style, or quality disputes between agencies and the enterprise program.

headings.title: Sale of office furniture under payment plan agreements
headings.reviewNote: Permits selling office systems and furniture to state agencies or political subdivisions outright or via payment plans contingent on fund solvency, with OA facilities division approval for OA-controlled or -leased state office space.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory purchase of vocational enterprise goods by state agencies, nonavailability certificates, pricing rules, arbitration, and furniture installment sales.

headings.title: Promotion of vocational enterprise products and services
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to develop marketing and promotional programs for products and services produced by vocational enterprises.

headings.title: Annual descriptive catalog of available vocational products
headings.reviewNote: Requires the vocational enterprises program to publish an annual descriptive catalog of styles, designs, and goods available for the year.

headings.title: Annual estimates of needs by public institutions
headings.reviewNote: Requires state agencies and political subdivisions to report annual purchasing estimates to the enterprise program by July first.

entries.reviewSummary: Promotion of correctional industry products, publication of annual descriptive catalogs, and annual agency purchasing estimates.

headings.title: Lease of correctional buildings for plasmapheresis program
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to lease buildings and access land at correctional centers to private entities for operating plasmapheresis programs.

headings.title: Inmate employment and discharge by plasmapheresis company
headings.reviewNote: Permits private plasmapheresis operators to employ and discharge selected offenders from the host correctional center with director approval.

headings.title: Director authority over facilities and offenders preserved
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the complete administrative authority of the director over correctional centers and confined offenders.

headings.title: Classification of plasmapheresis program as vocational enterprise
headings.reviewNote: Designates private plasmapheresis operations within correctional centers as recognized vocational enterprises.

entries.reviewSummary: Authority to lease correctional facility space for private plasmapheresis programs, inmate employment, and vocational enterprise status.

headings.title: Working capital revolving fund established in treasury
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Working Capital Revolving Fund as a revolving fund in the state treasury for vocational enterprise operations.

headings.title: Deposits from disposal of plants and machinery
headings.reviewNote: Directs that all funds derived from the disposal of plants and machinery under chapters 217 and 558 be deposited to the credit of the working capital revolving fund.

headings.title: Allowable expenditures from revolving fund for operations
headings.reviewNote: Directs use of the fund for establishing, maintaining, rehabilitating, expanding, and operating vocational enterprises, including machinery, raw materials, farm items, repairs, offender labor, administration, and training.

headings.title: Accrual basis enterprise accounting and reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires vocational enterprises to be accounted for on an accrual basis as an enterprise fund, with financial reports rendered to the director as required.

headings.title: Retention of earnings and charging of net losses
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits transferring enterprise earnings to general revenue at the end of each fiscal year, retains earnings for expansion and offender employment goals, and charges any net loss against the fund.

headings.title: Annual state auditor audit and report
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state auditor to audit the working capital revolving fund at the end of each fiscal year and report findings to the director, governor, and general assembly.

headings.title: Dissolution and transfer of vocational training fund
headings.reviewNote: Dissolves the vocational education and training fund effective August 28, 1994, and transfers all credited funds to the working capital revolving fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Working Capital Revolving Fund creation, receipts and plant disposal deposits, authorized expenditures, accrual accounting, fiscal-year retention, annual audit, and 1994 fund transfer.

headings.title: Parole board release duties and division supervision
headings.reviewNote: Charges the parole board with determining parole or conditional release under section 558.011 independently while cooperating systemically, with administrative support and circuit court supervision from the division of probation and parole.

headings.title: Adoption of parole guidelines and objectives
headings.reviewNote: Requires the parole board to adopt parole guidelines to preserve prison capacity for serious/violent offenders, release supervision-manageable cases, use validated risk/needs assessments, support reentry, set conditions, and respond to violations.

headings.title: Data analysis and agency performance measures
headings.reviewNote: Requires the parole board to collect, analyze, and apply data and establish performance and outcome measures for release decisions, supervision, revocation, recidivism, and caseloads.

headings.title: Publication of parole data and metrics
headings.reviewNote: Requires the parole board to publish parole data including grant rates, revocation and recidivism rates, length of time served, successful completions, and other performance metrics.

headings.title: Chairperson staffing, appointing authority, and training
headings.reviewNote: Requires the parole board chairperson to employ necessary staff, serve as appointing authority, and provide appropriate training to members and staff including communication skills.

headings.title: Division of probation and parole programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division of probation and parole to provide programs necessary to carry out its responsibilities consistent with its goals and statutory obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Parole board release authority and independence, parole guidelines, data analysis and public reporting, staff employment and training, and probation and parole division programs.

headings.title: Seven-member parole board appointed by governor
headings.reviewNote: Establishes, beginning August 28, 1996, a seven-member parole board appointed by the governor with senate advice and consent.

headings.title: Qualifications and bipartisan composition of parole board
headings.reviewNote: Requires board members to possess recognized decision-making qualifications and limits representation to no more than four members of the same political party.

headings.title: Six-year terms and reappointment of board members
headings.reviewNote: Provides six-year terms for successor board members until a successor is appointed and qualified, and permits members to be appointed to succeed themselves.

headings.title: Filling of board vacancies for unexpired terms
headings.reviewNote: Directs that vacancies occurring on the board be filled by gubernatorial appointment for the remainder of unexpired terms.

headings.title: Designation of board chair and vice chair
headings.reviewNote: Directs the governor to designate a chair and vice chair, authorizing the chair to supervise performance and assign duties.

headings.title: Full-time service and constitutional oath of office
headings.reviewNote: Requires board members to devote full time to official duties and take the constitutional oath of office filed with the secretary of state.

headings.title: Annual compensation and expense reimbursement for members
headings.reviewNote: Sets annual compensation ($45,000 plus section 105.005 adjustments for terms before Aug. 28, 1999; section 105.950 for later terms, with source Revisor's note referencing Appendix E) and section 33.090 expense reimbursement.

headings.title: Special retirement consultants for former board members
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes former board members who served prior to July 1, 2000, to act as special retirement consultants with preserved sick leave credits.

entries.reviewSummary: Composition of seven-member parole board, gubernatorial appointments, qualifications, six-year terms, chair duties, and compensation.

headings.title: Official seal of the parole board
headings.reviewNote: Requires the parole board to adopt an official seal of which courts shall take official judicial notice.

headings.title: Majority vote by hearing panels and appeals
headings.reviewNote: Requires majority votes by hearing panels for parole decisions, permitting board member referrals and thirty-day administrative appeals to the full board.

headings.title: Finality and judicial review limits of board orders
headings.reviewNote: Provides that board orders are not reviewable by courts except for compliance with statutory parole provisions and rules.

headings.title: Recordkeeping of board acts and facility notifications
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to maintain official records of its actions and notify correctional centers of release decisions.

headings.title: Closed meetings, records, and votes authorized
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes closed meetings, records, and votes for proceedings involving probation, parole, or pardon determinations.

headings.title: Videoconferencing for parole hearings and victim attendance
headings.reviewNote: Permits conducting parole and revocation hearings by videoconference, preserving victim attendance and barring videoconferencing upon victim objection.

entries.reviewSummary: Parole board hearing panel operations, majority votes, appeals, closed meetings, official seal, and videoconferencing procedures.

headings.title: Board headquarters barred from correctional center sites
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits locating the office and headquarters of the parole board on the site of any correctional center.

headings.title: Space provided in correctional centers for hearings
headings.reviewNote: Requires correctional centers to provide suitable space for offender interviews and hearings in their administration buildings.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibition on locating parole board headquarters on a correctional center site and requirement for interview and hearing space in correctional administration buildings.
